title: T1133 — External Remote Services
subtitle: Stolen credentials meet an unmonitored VPN portal.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Preparation
steps.caption: The attacker buys leaked employee credentials and scans the company's VPN portal.
steps.defender: scan-like traffic against your VPN from hosting providers is an early warning worth alerting on.

steps.title: Credential stuffing
steps.caption: Dozens of password attempts run against one account from 198.51.100.24 - the VPN logs every failure.
steps.defender: many failures from one IP followed by quiet is the classic stuffing signature.

steps.title: Success
steps.caption: One reused password works. The gateway opens a session without any MFA challenge - the account was excluded during a rollout.
steps.defender: fail-then-success from one IP must page someone, every time.

steps.title: First touch
steps.caption: The attacker lands on a corporate laptop over the VPN tunnel. It looks like a normal remote session.
steps.defender: new device fingerprint or country for this user should combine with the login anomaly.

steps.title: Detection
steps.caption: The SOC correlates the VPN anomaly with impossible travel - the same user had a local badge login minutes earlier.
steps.defender: impossible travel needs both sources: VPN logs and physical/badge or workstation events.
